title: fix(types): a write to a registered object whose table is missing answers 500 DATABASE_ERROR, as the read does, not 404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DJwKZqSF8gKyXHHSquun4GK)_

Fixes #27702

## What changes

The shared data-error classification (`packages/types/src/data-error-classification.ts`, `classifyDataError`) no longer answers a driver's missing-relation line (`no such table: …`, Postgres `relation "…" does not exist`) with `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` "Object '…' is not registered" when the relation names the request's object. Every missing-relation line is now the sanitised, logged `500 DATABASE_ERROR` (`DATA_STORE_FAULT`), the verdict the SQL driver already declares at its read exits for the same table. The attribution helper `missingRelationIsObject` had no other reader and is removed.

`404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` for an unregistered object is unchanged: its source is the structured `code: 'OBJECT_NOT_FOUND'` that the protocol's `assertObjectRegistered` and the engine's name resolution (`resolveObjectName`) throw before any driver sees the name, and the classification matches that arm far above the text limbs.

## Why

Measured on `origin/main` 81d00a4e with a real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver` + protocol + `RestServer`, an object registered after the DDL (its table never created), on better-sqlite3 and on a live PostgreSQL 16:

| door | producer of the answer | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /data/:object`, `GET /data/:object/:id` | driver-sql's declared read-exit fault (`backendStatementFault`) | `500 DATABASE_ERROR` | `500 DATABASE_ERROR` |
| `POST /data/:object` | the boundary's text classification of the raw driver error | `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` | `500 DATABASE_ERROR` |
| `PATCH` / `DELETE /data/:object/:id` | — | — | `500 DATABASE_ERROR` |
| unregistered object, `POST` and `GET` | registry gate | `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` | `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND` |

The PM's second hypothesis (the objectql insert path re-throwing the registry's "is not registered" error) was falsified: the insert leaves the dialect error undeclared (driver-sql's `backendStatementFault` docblock says the write paths are classified at the boundary on purpose), and the 404 came from the classifier's missing-relation limb. The fix is that one place, so no second copy of the rule exists and `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` is untouched. No new error code: `DATABASE_ERROR` is an existing catalog code.

## Verification

- New pin `packages/rest/src/data-door-missing-relation-registered-object.test.ts` (SQLite cell always; live Postgres cell under `OS_TEST_POSTGRES_URL`, a named skip otherwise): POST, PATCH and DELETE answer what GET answers, never `OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`; control: an unregistered object is still `404` on both doors. Run first against the unfixed classifier: **4 red** (the insert cell and the agreement cell, on both SQLite and live PG 16; the POST answered `404 OBJECT_NOT_FOUND`), 6 green. With the fix: 12/12 green on both cells.
- Pins that asserted the old 404 for a driver missing-table line were rewritten to the new verdict: `rest-unknown-object-heuristic.test.ts` (§2 attribution cells, §3 driver limb, the quiet-404 route cell now uses the gate's error, §5d), `rest.test.ts` (gate vs. driver envelope), `core/src/utils/import-runner-sandbox-fault-row.test.ts` (the #22868 control). A stale comment in `qa/http-conformance` was corrected.
- `@objectstack/types` 809/809, `@objectstack/rest` full run (local + repo projects) green after the `rest.test.ts` rewrite, `@objectstack/core` 2962/2962.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 62 families; all ran plus `pnpm lint` (results in the report comment). `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 3 (needs every package's dist) — NOT MEASURED.
